examples.label: Discharge date is 7 days before admission date

original_record.diagnosis_description: Urinary tract infection, site not specified

suggestions.explanation: discharge_date must be on or after admission_date. A negative length-of-stay is clinically impossible and will cause billing rejections, DRG miscalculation, and audit failures.
suggestions.how_to_fix: admission_date (2024-08-15) and discharge_date (2024-08-08) appear to be swapped — they are only 7 day(s) apart. Try reversing the two values. If the dates are not swapped, verify the source document.
suggestions.reference: CMS Conditions of Participation §482.24(c)(2)(vii); NUBC UB-04 billing form fields FL6/FL16

field_corrections.note: Dates appear swapped — admission and discharge values transposed
Dates appear swapped — admission and discharge values transposed

examples.label: patient_age is 52 but actual age from dates is 34

suggestions.violation_message: Stated age (52) does not match computed age (34) from date_of_birth (1990-04-10) and admission_date (2024-11-03)
suggestions.explanation: The stated patient_age does not match the age computed from date_of_birth and admission_date. This inconsistency can cause dosing errors, incorrect age-based treatment protocols, and billing rejections.
suggestions.how_to_fix: Set patient_age to 34. This is the exact age computed from the stored date_of_birth (1990-04-10) at the time of admission (2024-11-03).
suggestions.reference: HL7 FHIR R4 §Patient.birthDate; CMS Conditions of Participation §482.24(c)

examples.label: Osteoporosis diagnosis on a 5-year-old patient

original_record.diagnosis_description: Age-related osteoporosis without current pathological fracture

suggestions.violation_message: Diagnosis M81.0 is adult-only but patient age is 5
suggestions.explanation: Certain ICD-10 codes are age-restricted. Assigning an adult-only code to a paediatric patient (or vice versa) causes claim denials, incorrect quality-measure attribution, and may trigger fraud reviews.
suggestions.how_to_fix: Diagnosis code M81.0 is documented as adult-only (age ≥18). The patient's age is 5. Either: (a) verify the diagnosis — paediatric patients rarely present with M81.0; (b) correct patient_age if it was entered incorrectly; or (c) use the appropriate paediatric equivalent ICD-10 code.
suggestions.reference: ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines §Section I.C — Age/Sex Edits; CMS NCCI edits

field_corrections.note: M81.0 is restricted to patients ≥18; patient_age=5

fixed_record.diagnosis_description: Age-related osteoporosis without current pathological fracture

examples.label: Approval date is 3 weeks before application date

suggestions.violation_message: Approval date (2024-06-28) is before application date (2024-07-20)
suggestions.explanation: A loan cannot be approved before it is applied for. Temporal inconsistency in loan dates violates RESPA and TILA disclosure timeline requirements and may trigger regulatory audit flags.
suggestions.how_to_fix: approval_date (2024-06-28) is 22 days before application_date (2024-07-20). A loan cannot be approved before it is applied for. Verify both dates from the origination system. If the loan has not yet been decided, set approval_date to null.
suggestions.reference: CFPB TILA-RESPA Integrated Disclosure (TRID) §1026.19; Regulation B §1002.9 — timing of notifications

field_corrections.note: approval_date must be on or after application_date

examples.label: Loan amount is 52x annual income

suggestions.violation_message: Loan amount ($2,500,000) is 52.1x annual income ($48,000), exceeds 10.0x limit
suggestions.explanation: The loan-to-income ratio exceeds the 10× threshold. Extreme LTI ratios indicate the applicant cannot service the debt from income alone and violate CFPB Ability-to-Repay (ATR) standards, making the loan ineligible for QM safe-harbour protection.
suggestions.how_to_fix: Current ratio is 52.1× ($2,500,000 loan / $48,000 income). The maximum allowed is 10.0×. Either reduce loan_amount to ≤$480,000, or verify that annual_income reflects all qualifying income sources (co-applicant, rental income, bonuses). If a co-applicant exists, set co_applicant=true and add their income to annual_income.
suggestions.reference: CFPB Regulation Z §1026.43(c) — Ability-to-Repay; Fannie Mae Selling Guide B3-6-02 (debt-to-income ratios)

examples.label: 24-year-old claims 18 years of employment (would have started at age 6)

suggestions.violation_message: Employment length (18 years) is impossible for applicant age 24 (max possible: 8 years, assuming work starts at 16)
suggestions.explanation: employment_length_years exceeds what is possible given the applicant's age. This typically indicates a data entry error (e.g., total career years instead of current employer tenure) or identity fraud (age and employment don't match).
suggestions.how_to_fix: employment_length_years (18) exceeds the maximum possible for an applicant aged 24 (max: 8 years, assuming work starts at age 16). Correct the value to reflect verified employment history. If the applicant has had multiple employers, use the total cumulative years, capped at the computed maximum.
suggestions.reference: FLSA Child Labour Provisions §29 CFR Part 570 (minimum working age 16); CFPB ATR §1026.43(c)(3) — employment income verification

field_corrections.note: Applicant is 24 years old; max employment since age 16 = 8 years

examples.label: HC-002-example

suggestions.violation_message: Admission date (2024-09-14) is before date of birth (2025-03-15)
suggestions.explanation: A patient cannot be admitted before they were born. This error typically indicates a transposed year, a future date_of_birth, or an admission date entered for the wrong calendar year.
suggestions.how_to_fix: admission_date precedes date_of_birth, which is impossible. Either the admission_date is wrong (verify the calendar date of admission) or date_of_birth is wrong (verify the patient's birth record).
suggestions.reference: HL7 FHIR R4 §Patient.birthDate; Joint Commission Record of Care RC.02.01.01

field_corrections.note: admission_date must be on or after date_of_birth

examples.label: HC-005-example

suggestions.violation_message: Medication 'Metoprolol' is not a typical treatment for diagnosis category N39 (N39.0)
suggestions.explanation: 'Metoprolol' is not a recognised treatment for diagnosis category N39 (N39.0). Medication-diagnosis mismatches can indicate data entry errors, copy-paste mistakes from a previous record, or — rarely — a genuine off-label use that should be documented explicitly.
suggestions.how_to_fix: Verify the prescribed medication against the patient's chart for diagnosis N39.0. If the medication is correct (e.g., off-label use), add a clinical note to the record. Expected first-line options: Ciprofloxacin, Nitrofurantoin, Trimethoprim.
suggestions.reference: ISMP Medication Safety Alert — Drug-Disease Contraindications; Joint Commission NPSG.03.04.01 (medication reconciliation)

field_corrections.note: Typical first-line medications for N39 (N39.0): Ciprofloxacin, Nitrofurantoin, Trimethoprim

examples.label: FN-003-example

suggestions.violation_message: Existing debt ($50,000) is 83% of annual income ($60,000), exceeds 60% threshold
suggestions.explanation: Existing debt is 83.3% of annual income, above the 60% warning level. High DTI is the leading predictor of default. This record should receive manual underwriter review before proceeding.
suggestions.how_to_fix: existing_debt ($50,000) is 83% of annual_income ($60,000), exceeding the 60% warning threshold. This is a warning, not a hard block. Options: (1) verify that existing_debt only includes monthly obligations × 12 (not one-time balances); (2) check whether debt consolidation or payoff is planned before closing; (3) flag for manual underwriter review.
suggestions.reference: CFPB QM Standard — Back-End DTI ≤43% for Safe Harbour; Fannie Mae DU DTI limit §B3-6-02

examples.label: FN-005-example

suggestions.violation_message: Approved amount ($400,000) exceeds requested loan amount ($320,000)
suggestions.explanation: approved_amount ($400,000) exceeds the requested loan_amount ($320,000) by $80,000. A lender cannot approve more than was requested without issuing a counter-offer notice. This is a RESPA/TILA disclosure violation.
suggestions.how_to_fix: Set approved_amount to ≤$320,000 (the requested loan_amount). If the lender intends to offer more than requested (e.g., offering $400,000 when only $320,000 was asked), this requires a separate counter-offer disclosure under Regulation B §1002.9.
suggestions.reference: CFPB Regulation B (ECOA) §1002.9 — counter-offer notification; RESPA §12 CFR Part 1024 — settlement cost disclosures
